name: secret-list
title: Secret List
description: SecretList: stored secrets, like API keys, as rows with their name, a SecretFingerprint (•••• abcd), a configured or missing StatusPill, created, updated and last-used dates, and Replace and Delete. The data type has no value field. Loading, empty and error come through DataState. With selectable, each row gets a checkbox (disabled with a reason per secret) and an optional tri-state select all. Agents can replace and delete by id (delete waits for a person), and select by name or id.
docs:
`<SecretList aria-label="API keys" secrets={secrets} status={status} error={error} onRetry={refetch} onReplace={(id) => setReplacing(id)} onDelete={(id) => api.delete(id)} text={{ configured: "Configured", missing: "Missing", replace: "Replace", delete: "Delete", updated: (time) => <>Updated {time}</>, … }} />`.

A `StoredSecret` is `{ id, name, configured, fingerprint?, description?, createdAt?, updatedAt?, lastUsedAt? }` and has no value field: the list can't show a value because it never gets one. `fingerprint` is whatever few characters your server derives, like the last four, shown through `SecretFingerprint` after a mask and read as "Hidden value ending in a1b2" (`labels.fingerprint`); a configured secret without one shows the mask alone, and a missing one no mask, a warning status and `text.set` on its replace button. `lastUsedAt: null` shows `text.neverUsed`. Dates are RelativeTimes, by `locale`.

Replace runs `onReplace(id)`: open a `FormDialog` with `<FormField name="value"><Input sensitive revealable /></FormField>`, which never puts the new value in the DOM and clears it once saved. Delete opens a ConfirmDialog whose confirm button carries `data-agent-confirm` (`text.deleteAgentConfirm`) and runs `onDelete(id)`, pending while its Promise runs. Agents read the secrets as the list's items, by id and name, and call `replace(id)` and `delete(id)`, which opens the confirmation, so the delete itself waits for a person; an unknown id, or an action without its callback, fails the step with why.

Rows are a List rather than a DataTable: a handful of secrets with two actions each read better as rows that stack on a phone than as columns, and each row's buttons are named for its secret. Every visible word comes from `text`; `labels` holds the screen-reader names, in English by default.

**Per secret.** Delete shows on configured secrets only (an agent's `delete` of a missing one fails with why). `deleteTitle`, `deleteDescription`, `deleteConfirm` and `deleteAgentConfirm` take a string or a function of the secret, to name it: `deleteTitle: (secret) => "Delete " + secret.name`. The button of a missing secret holds `text.set` (falling back to `text.replace`) and is named by `labels.setSecret(name)`, "Set GitHub token", so its name matches what it says.

**Selection.** `selectable` gives each row a checkbox named by the secret, before its content; `selected`/`defaultSelected` hold the ids and `onSelectedChange(ids, details)` reports them (`details.reason` is `press`, `select-all` or `imperative`, and `details.cancel()` keeps the old ones). A secret with `disabled: { reason }` (or `true`) can't be selected: its checkbox is off, and the reason shows in the row and describes the checkbox. `text.selectAll` adds a checkbox above the rows, checked, unchecked or mixed, that selects or clears every secret that can be selected and leaves disabled ones as they are. Replace and Delete keep working beside the selection.

Agents call `select(nameOrId, checked = true)`, by the secret's name in any case or its id, and `selectAll(checked)`, and read `selected` (the names) and `selectedIds` in the snapshot. An unknown name, a disabled secret (with its reason), a list that isn't `selectable` or a change the app cancels fails the step with why. The row checkboxes carry `data-agent-hidden`, so agents use the list's actions and hear those reasons.
